question.text: Lotus Capital AIF, a Category II fund, has raised a corpus of INR 800 crore. Mr. Aditya Mehra, the sponsor, is finalising his 'continuing interest' contribution to satisfy Regulation 10(d) of SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012. What is the minimum sponsor commitment he must bring in?

answer.text: 2.5% of corpus or INR 5 crore, whichever is LOWER — i.e., INR 5 crore
2.5% of corpus or INR 5 crore, whichever is HIGHER — i.e., INR 20 crore
5% of corpus or INR 10 crore, whichever is lower — i.e., INR 10 crore
0.5% of the amount invested or INR 50 thousand, whichever is higher

explanation.text: **The Logic:** For Category I and II AIFs, the Sponsor/Manager continuing interest is not less than 2.5% of the corpus OR INR 5 crore, whichever is LOWER. On INR 800 crore corpus: 2.5% = INR 20 crore; the lower of (20 cr, 5 cr) = INR 5 crore. This is a floor-cap mechanism that keeps skin-in-the-game material but manageable for large funds. **The Trap:** The 'higher' variant swaps the rule — a very common confusion that traps candidates who forget the regulatory relief for large funds. The 5%/INR 10 cr option invents numbers. The 0.5%/INR 50k option is the Angel Fund rule, not Cat I/II. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests the same rule across all categories (Cat III sponsor commitment is 5% or INR 10 cr, whichever LOWER — note Cat III is a DIFFERENT number). XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) tests it from the LP disclosure angle. XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) uses the Cat III variant. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** As a Cat I/II manager, if your fund size grows post-first-close (e.g., green shoe from 500 cr to 1000 cr), you may need to top up sponsor commitment in subsequent tranches to maintain the 2.5%-or-5-cr-lower threshold. Plan liquidity for this — sponsor capital is locked in till final distribution.
